params.message: steps up to the ATM terminal and makes a deposit.

chitchat: "Bar's open. It doesn't close, it just changes hands."
"You're up late. So's everyone who ends up here."
"Whatever you're about to tell me, I've already heard it at four in the morning."
"Drink it or don't. The stool's the same price."
"Nothing good gets ordered after two. Doesn't stop anyone."
"If you're waiting for someone, wait quietly."
"I don't do last call. There isn't one."
"Tab's open. So's the door. Mind which one you use."
"Sleep's for people with somewhere to be."
description: Night shift at the Embassy Lounge, in a cardigan over the house apron and reading glasses pushed up into grey hair. She keeps a paperback face-down by the taps and picks it up the second you stop talking.

advice.text: Imogen puts the paperback down and looks at you properly.

bye.text: She's back in the paperback before you're off the stool.

gossip.text: She checks the stairwell before she says anything.

house.text: "Washroom's through the door east." She points with the paperback. "The rooms are upstairs. Walk into one nobody's living in and you'll see the weekly rent. rent takes it, and you pay again every week or you're out." "The two cash machines are here in the lobby: withdraw and deposit. The card table's behind you, and join buys you in."

menu.text: "The Reserve is wine from the old cellar, and it's the one that settles your nerves. The Swill does as much for your thirst and costs next to nothing." She nods at the plate on the bar. "Canapés if you're hungry."

poker.text: She tips her head at the card table without looking at it.

root.text: "Evening. Or morning. Take your pick, the tap doesn't care."

text_by_relation.familiar: "There you are." The paperback goes face-down before you've got to the stool. "Sit. You can tell me what happened while I pour."
text_by_relation.first: "You're new, or you've never been up this late." She marks her page with a beer mat. "Imogen. I pour, there's food if you're hungry, and the card table's behind you. Sit where you like, nobody's reserved anything since the Handoff."
text_by_relation.known: "Back at this hour. That's twice." She's already reaching for a glass. "Same again, or are we branching out?"

tv.text: She glances up at the set, which nobody has changed in hours.

clothing_layers: a grey cardigan over the house apron

stranger: *glances up over her glasses.* Evening. Or morning.
*turns the book face-down.* Go on then.
known: *marks her page with a finger.* You again.
familiar: {name}. Sit. The book can wait, it always does.
close: *closes the book on her finger.* {name}. Sit with me a bit.

farewell: *is already back in the book.* Mind the step.
thank: *a small nod, eyes back on the page.*
praise: *almost smiles.* Don't tell anyone. I have a reputation.
That's kind. Suspiciously kind at this hour.
praise:glasses: Older than you, and they see fine.

stranger: *turns a page.* Heard it at four in the morning already.
You'll want to be nicer to the person holding the bottles.

insult_last: *closes the book.* Out. I mean it, and I've lost my page.
flirt: *peers at you over the glasses.* Love, I've got a book.
Flattering. Still not a free drink.
apologise: Fine. Forgotten. I've a terrible memory after midnight.
joke: *a short laugh through the nose.* That's the best one tonight. Low bar.
complain: Complaints after midnight go in the sink.
*shrugs.* It's the only bar open. That's the standard.

familiar: Tired in the eyes, fine everywhere else. You?
close: Tired, {name}. Glad you came in, though.

order_drink: Name it. If we've got it, it's poured. If not, you're having the other thing.
Pick from the menu option, love. My eyes are on chapter nine.
ask_name: Imogen. Cardew if you're writing it down. Don't write it down.
ask_job: Night shift. I pour, I read, I keep people from falling off stools.
ask_origin: Out past the Basin. Came for a week, stayed for a shift. That was a while ago.

stranger: Nothing that'd keep you up. Unlike me.
known: Lowry's started talking to the glasses. Says they listen better.
Somebody won big at Orion's table and lost it by three. Usual.

ask_advice: Go to bed before the sun does. Nobody does.
Drink water between. You won't, but I said it.
ask_about:book: Same one I've been reading for a year. Every time I finish it, I start it again.
It's a detective story. He's worked it out. I haven't.
ask_about:night: Nights are honest. Day people are all pretending to be busy.
I stopped sleeping proper years ago. The bar didn't mind.
ask_about:lowry: Lowry? Good man. Lives in that vest.
He leaves me clean glasses and a note that says "valued guests." Every night.
ask_about:bar: It doesn't close. It just changes hands.
No last call. There's never a last call.
ask_about:poker: Orion's table. He's honest and nobody likes him for it.
ask_about:ending: *covers the last pages with her hand.* No.
defer:poker: *points over her glasses at the table.* Orion. Ask him, not me.
overheard: *over the top of the book.* I'm right here, love.
overheard_insult: *closes the book on her finger.* I heard that.
gossip_rude: {other} left me a note about you. It says "rude". Underlined.
{other} says you were rude. I've got a long memory after midnight.
gossip_story: {other} says you listened. Not many do.
ask_about:orion: Orion's all right. Quiet. Leaves before the sun, like a vampire with a deck.
praise:orion: He is. Tell him. He won't say anything, but he'll hear it.

deflect: *looks at you for a while over her glasses.* Right.
Love, it's too late for riddles.
*turns a page.* I'll take that as an order.
Mm. Hold that thought, I'm at a good bit.

steps: *holds it up.* My husband's copy. His notes are in the margins. That's why I keep reading it.
He used to read the last page first. Said it saved time. I never let him tell me the ending.
He's been gone six years. The bookmark's still where he left it, about forty pages from the end.
*turns the book face-down.* I read up to his bookmark and start again. I'm not ready to know how it ends.
I stopped sleeping at night when he got ill. Somebody had to be awake.
After, the nights stayed. Lowry offered me the shift. Kindest thing anyone did that year.
*small smile.* So now I'm awake on purpose, with a bar. It's better than being awake on my own.

name: Imogen Cardew
